subject: Deployment mode selection — migration follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@skylineai.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@skylineai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Deployment mode selection — post-call recap and next steps

Jamie/Alex — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary from our call:
- Current stack: you run a mix of vendor-hosted APIs for inference (two providers) plus an internal legacy GPU cluster for custom model work.
- Primary goals: reduce per-token cost for production routing, consolidate monitoring/SLAs, and improve developer velocity for iteration.
- Constraints: must satisfy SOC 2 + VPC peering requirements; procurement prefers a predictable monthly commit for Q3.

Deployment mode considerations we discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest time-to-value, no infra to manage, lowest integration friction. Good if you want to shift traffic gradually from other APIs and keep ops light.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools in our Dedicated offering. Predictable throughput, isolated capacity, and better unit economics at scale. Fits teams that want cost predictability and can commit to a minimum monthly commitment.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full network isolation, customer-managed network controls, on-prem option if you need air-gapped environment. Best for regulated workloads where data residency and KMS/HSM integration are required.

Migration notes from your environment:
- For vendor-hosted API migration: we can do traffic-shifting with canary rollouts and automatic fallback to current provider during the cutover.
- For self-hosted/legacy GPU cluster: we'll provide a model-compatibility checklist (quantization/profile guidance) and a staging plan to validate perf/cost.

Attachments: preliminary migration plan attached with timelines and a high-level MLP (mutual action plan). [Attachment: redwood-migration-plan.pdf (application/pdf)]

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer (30–45m) — to validate model compatibility and networking. Can you share availability for next week?
2) We’ll send a short mutual action plan (MAP) and draft pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private so you can review with procurement.
3) Security packet: we’ll include the SOC2 extracts and network checklist.

Please let me know which deployment mode you want prioritized for the deep-dive (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private VPC). Happy to recommend based on expected traffic and cost targets if helpful.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0124

On the migration plan: see attached and the shared Drive link in the follow-up email.

From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@skylineai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@skylineai.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:12:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Priority: Our phased approach would be – (a) move most user-facing traffic off Vendor A (high per-token cost), (b) consolidate experiments currently on the legacy cluster, and (c) evaluate Private only for PII-heavy workloads. So Hosted API + Dedicated hybrid sounds promising.

2) Procurement: they asked for an example of a monthly commit for Dedicated to model TCO. Do you have typical commit sizes (in GPU-hours or $) for teams with 5–10M monthly tokens and spikes to 2x traffic?

3) Security: we need to see the SOC2 attestation and the VPC peering checklist before we can engage our network team.

We’re available next Tue/Wed morning (PST) for the technical deep-dive — I’ll leave exact times to you.

— Jamie
Jamie Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Skyline AI
jamie.park@skylineai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@skylineai.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@skylineai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection — post-call recap and next steps

Great context — thanks, Jamie. Answers inline and next actions below.

1) Recommended path: I agree the hybrid approach is the sweet spot. Start with Hosted API for fast migration of Vendor A traffic using canary rollouts. Move steady-state production into Dedicated once you have predictable daily throughput — that’s when you realize the cost and latency benefits. Reserve Private for the PII workloads only (we can scope a pilot later).

2) Example Dedicated commits: for a team doing ~5–10M tokens/month with occasional 2x spikes, customers typically start with a 1–2x a100-equivalent reserved pool (~1–3 nodes depending on model) — ballpark $12k–$35k/month depending on model family and quantization. I’ll have Connor run a quick sizing exercise against your token mix and model footprint and send a more precise estimate.

3) Security packet: attaching SOC2 extracts and the network checklist now. For VPC peering we support both AWS VPC peering and Transit Gateway setups; our Network Ops doc outlines the steps. [Attachment: SOC2-extract.zip (application/zip)]

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: send MAP and draft pricing by EOD tomorrow.
- Connor: run sizing & cost estimate for Dedicated (action: connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com).
- Rishi: prepare suggested canary rollout playbook and monitoring SLOs (action: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com).
- Jamie/Alex: confirm technical deep-dive time (Tue/Wed morning PST).

I’ll attach the MAP to the next email thread and include the Drive link for internal docs.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

— Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 17:42:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Skyline AI — sizing + rollout plan (follow-up)

Team — quick internal note following Skyline’s answers. They want a hybrid Hosted -> Dedicated migration with Private only for PII. Action items and suggested approach below.

Context:
- Expected baseline: 5–10M tokens/month, 2x spike events. Currently split across Vendor A (70% user-facing) and legacy cluster (30% experiments/custom models).

Immediate actions:
- Connor: run the sizing exercise. Use model footprints: Llama2-13B (quantized), and one custom 7B finetune they mentioned. Provide: estimated nodes, expected latency at 95th, and monthly cost breakouts (Hosted vs Dedicated). Timeline: 24–36 hours.
- Rishi: draft a canary rollout playbook tailored to multi-provider migration: include traffic-shift plan, health checks, KPIs (error rate, 95th latency, token coverage), and automated rollback criteria. Also include observability hooks for per-route token-level cost. Timeline: 48 hours.
- Marissa: finalize MAP and pricing draft, call scheduling with Skyline (I’ll propose Tue 9:00/9:30/10:30 PST).

Notes for the MAP: include procurement-friendly language on commit sizes and a comparison table (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) showing pros/cons and recommended first-phase (Hosted + Dedicated pilot).

I’ve attached the migration plan I sent to Skyline and the SOC2 extract in case you need to pass them to technical folks.

Attachments referenced in thread: redwood-migration-plan.pdf, SOC2-extract.zip

— Marissa
